_comment: Configuration for check.py. Edit this rather than the script when the
business changes. Every value here is a fact about this repo, not about
canonical_source: the file the checker reads current facts out of. It is
the single source of truth for name, email and prices, and says so in its
own header comment. If that ever stops being true, this checker is wrong.
superseded_terms: names, domains and addresses the business used to use.
Finding one outside a historical path usually means a rename was left
half-done. Add to this list on the day a rename happens, not later.
historical_paths: files whose job is to record what happened. Old names and
old prices are CORRECT here and must not be 'fixed' — editing them destroys
the record of why a decision went the way it did. The session log, the
rename plan and delivered client audits are all in this category.
plan_aliases: how a plan gets named in prose, so a price sitting next to it
can be checked against the canonical number for that plan.
_external_files_note: Files the documents name on purpose that are not in this repo, so
the refs check does not report them as broken. Client audit data
lives in the client's own folder outside the repo — ops/audit-
method.md section 5 — so the per-run timings.md is meant to be absent.
_reviewed_dupes_note: Passages duplicated on purpose, by file pair, with the reason. checks.md
allows exactly one case: a banner repeated at the top of several entry
points so that no reader misses it. The rename banner is that case.
The exemption is conditional on the copies staying identical. While they
are, the finding drops to a note with the reason attached. The moment they
diverge it becomes an ERROR rather than the usual verify — a banner saying
different things in three places is worse than one written once, and it is
the specific failure this entry exists to catch.

_record_section_note: A heading matching this pattern marks a section whose job is to record a
price change, so the old prices inside it are correct and are skipped by
the facts check. It runs until the next heading of the same or higher
level, so subsections stay inside it.
Keep this narrow. A loose version ('any dated heading saying changed')
matched ROADMAP.md's 'What changed on 2026-08-06' — a section about the
present — and silently hid a stale price underneath it. A noisy finding
costs a glance; a suppressed one costs the whole point of the check.
_reviewed_names_note: File/term pairs judged correct as written, with the reason and the date the
judgement was made. The names check downgrades these to notes instead of
errors, so a later run does not re-investigate them from scratch.
This is a record of a decision, not a mute button: the mentions are still
printed with the reason attached. Delete an entry to put it back in front of
the reader — and do delete it if the file's purpose changes.

_superseded_prices_note: Prices this business has charged and stopped charging, from the repricing
records in ops/service-tiers.md sections 9 and 11. Any of these stated
outside a record section or a historical file is drift.
This exists because attribution is not enough. 'a stranger can read the site
and pay us £125' names no plan and holds one amount, so neither the
price-to-plan rule nor the ladder rule can see it — but £125 is a price this
250 is deliberately absent: it was Grow's old monthly price and is now the
audit's, so it cannot be judged from the number alone.
30 and 75 were dropped after they collided with supplier costs — a £30
Hoxton Mix plan is not our old audit price. Small round numbers are common
in other people's pricing, and both were retired at the first repricing
_reviewed_facts_note: Amounts that are correct as written but read as price drift, judged once so
they are not re-triaged every run. Keyed on file and amount, not line, so
they survive a condensing pass moving the text.
These only ever downgrade the 'verify' grade. An ERROR — a document stating a
price this business does not charge — can never be silenced from here. If a
fact is wrong, fix the fact.
